initiation.analysts: GAM Research — Oil, gas & consumable fuels

cover.headline: A record year at the top of the oil cycle, priced above what the market has paid for ONGC's core since 2021: SELL
cover.lead: ONGC produces 73% of India's crude and 57% of its gas, and owns 54.9% of HPCL, 71.6% of MRPL, 14.2% of Indian Oil, 12.5% of Petronet, 5% of GAIL and all of ONGC Videsh. The Strait of Hormuz crisis gave it a record Q1FY27 (standalone profit ₹17,034 cr, +112%) and no windfall tax followed. But FY27 is a peak: on the EIA's path Brent falls to ~US$70 by FY28E and our core profit (before dividends from the stakes) drops ~31%. We value ONGC the way the street does, as a **sum of the parts**, but with a **derived** multiple: 3.5x Sep-28E core profit (the market's own median since 2021, 3.3x, times the +2.2% sector move), plus the stakes at 30-Sep-2026 prices less a 20% holding discount, ONGC Videsh at ₹15 a share and the unlisted holdings at cost. **Target {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}. The street (median ₹296) uses 6.3-8x on similar earnings.

arguments.h: FY27 is a windfall, not a new level
arguments.p: Q1FY27 crude realisation was US$99.45 vs US$66.13 a year earlier; volumes fell 5%. We assume Brent US$90.5 in FY27E and US$69.5 in FY28E (EIA, Sep-2026): EPS ₹{{F.eps.0|n1}} then ₹{{F.eps.1|n1}}. Every US$1/bbl is worth ~₹978 cr of FY28E crude revenue after royalty and cess.

arguments.h: The market has rarely paid the street's multiple
arguments.p: After deducting the stakes at 80% of market value, ONGC Videsh and the unlisted holdings, the market has paid a median 3.3x forward core profit since Apr-2021. On 30-Sep-2026 it paid 4.2x on our Sep-28E core profit. The street's 6.3-8x was paid only briefly, in Mar-Sep 2024. Each half-turn on the core is ~₹14.9 a share.

arguments.h: The stakes are real value, discounted for good reason
arguments.p: The listed stakes are worth ₹80 a share (35% of ONGC's market value). Two of them, HPCL and MRPL, are refiners whose profits fall when crude spikes (HPCL lost ₹12,265 cr in Q1FY27). ONGC has never sold a share; we apply our house 20% discount for listed stakes inside an operating company (JM, BOB 20%; MOSL, PL 25%).

Brent staying near US$80-90 (management expects US$75+ long term), a fast gas ramp-up at KG-98/2 and Daman, or a market that finally pays 6-8x for the core as the street expects. Against that: a windfall tax, pressure to share OMC losses, and more state-directed spending. Dividend yield at our payout: ~8% on FY27E DPS, ~6% on FY28E, which supports the share price on the way down.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter with Brent falling from the Q1 peak, and the post-monsoon survey and dry-well costs.
Any windfall-tax or under-recovery-sharing decision while HPCL and the other fuel retailers lose money.
KG-98/2 gas wells hooked up after the CPP (management: Oct-Nov 2026) and the Daman Upside ramp-up to ~3 mmscmd by Dec-2026.
The first Mahanadi deepwater well under Samudra Manthan (spudded 25-Jul-2026, result expected about three months later).
The APM gas ceiling for FY28 and the formula price as crude falls; any OFS by the government (none announced).

sections.title: India's oil and gas producer, with a refining and marketing group attached

blocks.p: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) finds and produces crude oil and natural gas in India: 73% of the country's crude and 57% of its gas in FY26. Most of its output comes from "nomination" fields given to it before the 1999 bidding regime (NELP) began (Mumbai High and the Western Offshore, Gujarat, Assam, the KG and Cauvery basins), where the government sets the gas price and takes royalty and a cess on crude; a smaller part comes from its share of blocks bid under later contract regimes. It sells crude to refiners at Brent-linked prices, gas to GAIL and city-gas companies, and LPG, naphtha and ethane-propane from its processing plants. Its 1P reserves were 518 MMtoe at March 2026 (about 13 years of output). Around this core sits a group: **ONGC Videsh** (100%: overseas fields in 14 countries), **HPCL** (54.9%) and **MRPL** (71.6%) in refining and fuel retail, stakes in **Indian Oil** (14.2%), **GAIL** (5%) and **Petronet LNG** (12.5%), the loss-making **OPaL** petrochemical plant, and **ONGC Green** (renewables).

blocks.p: **Why we value the standalone company, not the group.** The consolidated accounts add HPCL and MRPL line by line: in FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹6,62,247 cr, five times standalone, and in Q1FY27 HPCL's ₹12,265 cr loss turned a ₹17,034 cr standalone profit into ₹6,554 cr for the group. Most brokers (JM, MOSL, PL, Geojit) value standalone earnings and add the stakes, and so do we; consolidated EPS appears only as context.

The corporate actions that moved value were acquisitions the government asked for (HPCL, OPaL) and policy changes (windfall tax, gas formula, royalty), not share-capital moves.

sections.title: A crude price set in the Gulf; a gas price set in Delhi

blocks.p: Brent averaged US$70.45/bbl in FY26 (US$78.91 in FY25) and traded US$60-70 for most of the year; the West Asia (Strait of Hormuz) crisis from March 2026 sent it to ~US$97-98 in Q1FY27 (ONGC call) and ~US$96 in Jul-Sep 2026. EIA (9-Sep-2026) expects ~US$90 in 2H2026, US$77 in Q2-2027 and ~US$67 in 2H2027 as shut-in output returns (2027 average US$74). India produced 27.95 MMT of crude (-2.6%) and 34.78 BCM of gas (-3.7%) in FY26; import dependence 88.7% (Mar-2026). ONGC: 73% of crude, 57% of gas (AR FY26).

Gas from old (nomination) fields is priced by formula with a cap (US$7.00/mmBtu in FY27 vs a US$9.00 formula price in Sep-2026), so ONGC does not keep the upside on ~76% of its gas; new-well gas (24% of Q1FY27 sales) gets 1.2x the formula price uncapped. Crude is sold at Brent-linked prices. Windfall tax (SAED) Jul-2022 to Dec-2024 took ₹23,800 cr from ONGC; not re-imposed by 30-Sep-2026. Royalty cut 8-May-2026 (offshore crude 9.09%->8%, gas 10%->8%). Samudra Manthan: ₹84,084 cr government deepwater exploration scheme.

blocks.callout: **So what:** ONGC is a price-taker on crude and a price-controlled seller of most of its gas. Its earnings respond to Brent with a lever the government holds at both ends: it cut royalty in May-2026 to encourage exploration, and it taxed windfalls in 2022-24. The share price on 30-Sep-2026 reflects the market's doubt about which hand will act next.

blocks.p: Every US$1/bbl on Brent is worth ~₹978 cr of crude revenue after royalty and cess in FY28E, or ~₹0.6 of EPS. Our FY28E Brent of US$69.5 versus FY27E's US$90.5 explains most of the fall in EPS from ₹{{F.eps.0|n1}} to ₹{{F.eps.1|n1}}. **Verdict: the 2026 windfall is reaching shareholders, but it is a one-year gift, not a re-rating of the business.**

sections.title: Crude: two-thirds of revenue from fields that need ever more capex to stand still

blocks.p: ONGC sold 18.79 MMT of crude in FY26 (incl. its JV share), against 21.34 MMT in FY20. The old giants of the Western Offshore (Mumbai High and its satellites) decline ~5-6% a year naturally; ONGC fights that with infill drilling, water injection and a technical-services partnership (TSP) with BP on Mumbai High, now extended to the whole Western Offshore, which management says now produces 107% of the contractual baseline for oil and 113% for gas. KG-DWN-98/2, the deepwater block that was meant to add growth, has disappointed on oil (~21,000 bbl/d; reservoir connectivity problems; each well re-entry costs >₹500 cr). Management guides oil about flat in FY27 and ~+0.5 MMT in FY28.

sections.title: Gas: the growth engine, priced by formula and capped

blocks.p: Gas was 27% of FY26 revenue (₹36,330 cr) and is where ONGC's volume growth will come from: Daman Upside (+2 mmscmd by Dec-2026), the East Coast CPP (1.3 mmscmd), Tapti/Daman wells (0.5) and KG-98/2 gas (from 1.5-1.7 to ~3 mmscmd by Q4FY27 and 6-7 by Q4FY28). Kirit Parikh formula since Apr-2023: APM gas = 10% of the Indian crude basket, floor US$4, ceiling US$6.50 rising US$0.25 a year from FY26: US$6.75 (FY26), US$7.00 (FY27). New-well gas from nomination fields gets a 20% premium. HPHT/deepwater ceiling US$8.9 for Apr-Sep 2026 (AR FY26 MD&A). In Q1FY27 the formula price was well above the cap, so old-well gas earned US$7 while new-well gas earned US$13.31 (₹3,998 cr of revenue, ₹1,897 cr above the APM price). New-well gas was 24% of sales volume (17% a year earlier) and 38% of gas revenue.

pair.title: Gas sold: down a fifth since FY20; new projects turn it up from FY28E
Average gas realisation: our path

blocks.callout: **So what:** at ~US$70 crude the APM formula (~US$7.0) falls to or below the ceiling (US$7.25 in FY28 if the US$0.25 a year step continues), so the cap stops costing ONGC much, but new-well gas also loses its Q1FY27 premium. Our FY28E gas revenue (₹43,812 cr) is below FY27E (₹45,702 cr) even with 5% more volume.

sections.title: ONGC Videsh is recovering; the listed stakes are worth ₹80 a share

blocks.p: **ONGC Videsh (OVL)** holds 29 projects in 14 countries and produced 9.67 MMTOE in FY26 (crude 6.91 MMT, gas 2.76 BCM: down from 8.10 MMT and 4.23 BCM in FY22: Sakhalin-1, its most important asset, was out of OVL's hands for about four years after Russia took the project over). The stake was restored in Dec-2025 and OVL now earns ~₹1,000-1,140 cr a quarter (₹2,260 cr in Q4FY26 before impairment), though price caps cut the realisation on Russian barrels. Mozambique LNG (first gas end-FY28/early FY29, ~3 MMTPA share), Brazil's BM-SEAL (first oil 2030) and Venezuela (OFAC licence obtained) are the options. We do not have OVL's audited book value in our sources, so we use the two broker values: JM (7x FY28E EPS, ₹7 a share) and MOSL (0.5x FY25 book, ₹23); base = midpoint ₹15.

blocks.p: The stakes pay ONGC dividends (₹4,807 cr in FY26, of which HPCL ₹1,811 cr), but ONGC has never sold them, and two (HPCL, MRPL) are refiners whose profits move opposite to ONGC's when crude spikes. That is a natural hedge for the group and a reason the market discounts them inside ONGC: an investor who wants HPCL can buy HPCL.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** Scale and incumbency in Indian upstream (73% of crude, 57% of gas; nomination acreage held since before 1999; 518 MMtoe of 1P reserves); but a price-taker on crude, a price-controlled seller on 76% of its gas, with mature fields declining 5-8% a year. No pricing power; the advantage is access to acreage and infrastructure, and the cost of capital of a sovereign-backed company. We score the moat AMBER: durable assets, no control over the price of what they produce.

sections.title: Standalone profit follows the oil price and the government's share of it, not volumes

blocks.p: ONGC's standalone revenue has moved between ₹68,000 cr (FY21, crude at US$45) and ₹1,44,500 cr (FY23, US$93) with almost no change in volume: crude sold fell every year, from 21.3 MMT in FY20 to 18.8 MMT in FY26, and gas from 19.4 to 15.5 BCM. Price did all the work. In FY26 revenue was ₹1,32,506 cr and net profit ₹32,894 cr (EPS ₹26.15), down 8% as Brent averaged US$70. Then the Strait of Hormuz crisis lifted Brent to ~US$97-98 in Q1FY27: revenue rose 45% to ₹46,460 cr and profit 112% to a record ₹17,034 cr in one quarter. **The so-what: a year of ONGC profit is mostly a bet on Brent and on how much of it the government lets ONGC keep.**

blocks.callout: **So what:** the government shares in ONGC's upside three times: royalty and cess (a fixed share of price), the APM gas cap (it keeps the formula price above US$7.00), and, when prices spike, an ad hoc windfall tax (₹23,800 cr in FY23-25). It did not re-impose the windfall tax in the 2026 spike (to 30-Sep-2026), and it cut royalty in May-2026. That is the single biggest reason FY27E earnings are high, and the single biggest risk to them.

sections.title: Half the cash goes back to shareholders; the rest into flat production and state-directed investments

blocks.p: ONGC spent ₹1,93,378 cr of capex in FY22-26 (₹35,878 cr in FY26; ₹62,057 cr in FY25 was a one-year peak) and declared ₹74,853 cr of dividends (DPS ₹10.50 to ₹13.25). The capex has held production flat, not grown it: standalone crude 19.5 MMT in FY22, 19.3 MMT in FY26. The large investments outside E&P were made at the government's direction: HPCL (₹36,915 cr, Jan-2018), OPaL (₹21,181 cr of equity, still loss-making in Q1FY27) and ONGC Green (₹4,700 cr).

blocks.callout: **Capital allocation verdict:** the dividend is reliable (it rose every year from FY21; FY26 paid out ₹16,669 cr, 51% of profit, through two interims and a final) and the balance sheet is strong. But the capital ONGC controls is not fully its own: the government, which owns 58.89%, has used it to buy HPCL, rescue OPaL and fund national exploration missions. Minority shareholders get the dividend; they do not decide where the rest goes.

blocks.callout: **Our accounting flag is AMBER.** Nothing is hidden, but reported profit is regularly moved by policy (windfall tax, royalty), tax-regime effects and impairments. In this report "core profit" is standalone profit before exceptional items and before dividends from the stakes, taxed at 25.17%.

sections.title: Net cash, with stakes worth ₹1 lakh crore and few debts

blocks.p: At March 2026 ONGC standalone had ₹28,660 cr of cash and bank balances against ₹7,823 cr of borrowings; the rest of Screener's ₹33,645 cr "borrowings" are lease liabilities (₹25,822 cr: rigs, vessels, offshore facilities). It also held ₹32,728 cr in a site-restoration fund (a ring-fenced deposit for decommissioning fields) and ₹1,13,379 cr of investments at book value (subsidiaries at cost, IOC and GAIL at fair value), whose market value was ~₹98,000 cr for the quoted ones (AR).

blocks.callout: **So what:** solvency is not a question. Two items deserve attention: contingent liabilities (the Panna-Mukta-Tapti arbitration alone is ~₹15,216 cr, where ONGC chose not to defend itself), and guarantees for subsidiaries (ONGC has guaranteed OPaL's debt to cut its funding cost). In the engine's forecast, "treasury" is cash plus investments at book less borrowings, so it is not all spendable cash.

sections.title: Management & governance: competent operators, short tenures, and the state as the real decision-maker

blocks.p: Arun Kumar Singh, Chairman & CEO (formerly CMD of BPCL), re-employed on contract for a further year from 7-Dec-2025 or until a regular incumbent takes charge, whichever is earlier. Anupam Agarwal, Director (Finance) from 3-Jun-2026. ONGC is a central public-sector enterprise: the Ministry of Petroleum appoints its board and its executives, and directives on investments (HPCL, OPaL), arbitration (Panna-Mukta-Tapti) and pricing come from government.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** honest accounts and generous dividends, but minority shareholders should assume that when national and shareholder interests diverge (fuel prices, windfall taxes, rescues), the national interest wins. That is the core of the discount the market applies.

blocks.p: **Against the street.** Broker EPS on 30-Sep-2026 is mostly consolidated, so it is not comparable with ours: JM ₹38.6 / ₹39.2 (FY27-28E, consolidated), BOB ₹40.3 / ₹40.5, PL ₹38.2 / ₹41.5 (consolidated). The comparable numbers are standalone: PL expects FY27E standalone PAT of ~₹51,160 cr (EPS ~₹40.7) against our ₹{{F.pat.0|num}} cr (PL's quarterly revenue path is close to ours; the gap is below EBITDA and its note does not split it); Geojit ₹40.2 / ₹33.1; JM's FY28E standalone core EPS (before dividends) is ₹29.2, close to our ₹29.5 (Sep-28E ₹29.9). **Our earnings are in line with the street for FY28E; the difference in our target is the multiple, not the profit.**

sections.title: The street: mostly Buy, median target ₹296 on 30-Sep-2026

blocks.p: Wide: S&P Global counted 31 analysts in Sep-2026 (18 strong buy, 5 buy, 4 hold, 3 sell, 1 strong sell). Notes we read or saw summarised from the Q1FY27 results cycle (4-31 Aug 2026): JM Financial, BOB Caps, Motilal Oswal, PL, ICICI Securities, Kotak, Geojit; target-only rows for Jefferies, JP Morgan, Nomura, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley (24-Sep). Mostly a sum of the parts: standalone earnings on a P/E of 6.3-8x (FY28E, Dec-27E or Jun-28E), plus the listed stakes at market less a 20-25% holding discount (Geojit 50%), and ONGC Videsh valued separately (JM 7x FY28E EPS = ₹7/share; MOSL 0.5x FY25 book = ₹23/share). BOB Caps applies 6.5x to consolidated EPS and adds only IOC, GAIL and Petronet. JM uses FY28E standalone EPS before dividend income ('core', ₹29.2). Crude: JM US$80 FY27E then US$70; MOSL US$80 rest of FY27 then US$75; BOB US$80; APM gas US$6.9-7.2. JM: the share price discounts ~US$60/bbl net because of windfall-tax fears; JM and CLSA see no windfall-tax risk.

blocks.p: The 12 targets set in Jul-Sep 2026 range from ₹230 (JP Morgan) to ₹365 (ICICI Securities); median ₹296. S&P Global's consensus of 29 analysts averaged ₹287 (labelled 24-Sep-2026; it may include later changes). The street's SOTPs agree on earnings (JM's FY28E core EPS ₹29.2 is within 5% of ours) and differ on the multiple: 6.3-8x standalone earnings, which ONGC has rarely been paid in the market since 2021 (see Valuation). Two foreign brokers cut to Hold after Q1 (JP Morgan to ₹230, Nomura to ₹265).

blocks.h: What the bears and bulls argue

bullets: **Bear:** Production has not grown in five years: standalone crude 19.3-19.6 MMT since FY22, gas down from 20.9 to 19.5 BCM; KG-98/2 oil has disappointed.
**Bear:** Policy takes the upside: windfall tax (₹23,800 cr in FY23-25), the APM cap, and pressure to share OMC losses (HPCL, its own subsidiary, lost ₹12,265 cr in Q1FY27).
**Bear:** Capital allocation is directed by the state: HPCL (₹36,915 cr in 2018), OPaL (₹21,181 cr invested, still loss-making in Q1FY27), and deepwater exploration under Samudra Manthan.
**Bear:** Consolidated earnings are hostage to OMC marketing margins; standalone is what most of the street values.
**Bear:** Contingent liabilities: Panna-Mukta-Tapti arbitration ₹15,216 cr where ONGC chose not to defend itself at the ministry's request.
**Bull:** no windfall tax was imposed in the 2026 spike, and royalty was cut: policy has turned friendlier to producers (JM, CLSA).
**Bull:** gas volumes turn up from H2FY27 (DUDP, KG-98/2 gas, CPP), and new-well gas earns uncapped prices.
**Bull:** a 6-8% dividend yield at our FY27-28E payout, and listed stakes worth ~35% of the market value.

sections.title: Valuation: the core at 3.5x, the stakes at market less 20%, gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}

blocks.p: The street values ONGC as a **sum of the parts (SOTP)**: standalone earnings on a P/E of 6.3-8x (JM 7x FY28E core EPS, MOSL 6.5x Dec-27E, PL 8x FY28E, Geojit 6.3x, BOB 6.5x on consolidated EPS), plus the listed stakes at market less a 20-25% holding discount (Geojit 50%), plus ONGC Videsh. We use the same structure. Two choices matter: we capitalise **core** profit (before the dividends the stakes pay, which would otherwise be counted twice, and before one-offs), and we **derive** the core multiple from what the market has actually paid for ONGC since 2021 rather than adopt a broker's multiple.

blocks.p: We add no separate net cash: interest on ONGC's ₹28,660 cr of cash and its site-restoration fund is inside core profit, and lease costs are inside it too. OPaL is in at ONGC's cost (₹21,181 cr), which is generous for a plant that lost money at EBITDA in Q1FY27; the bear case sets it to zero.

blocks.h: The core multiple: 3.5x Sep-28E core profit

blocks.p: ONGC has never traded without its stakes, so its own P/E history mixes the E&P business with HPCL, MRPL, IOC, GAIL and Petronet. We separate them the way our SOTP does: every week since April 2021 we take ONGC's market value, deduct the listed stakes at that week's prices less the same 20% discount, ONGC Videsh (₹15 a share) and the unlisted holdings at cost, and divide what is left by the next full year's core profit (actual, our estimates for FY27-28). That is the **implied forward P/E the market paid for the core business**.

blocks.p: **Reading the table.** Our base follows the rule (median since Apr-2021, no trough years). It is pulled down by two price spikes (forward years FY23 and FY27), when the market rightly refused to capitalise peak profit; leaving those weeks out, or starting in Apr-2023, gives ~4.5x and a HOLD-range target. We keep the rule: at 30-Sep-2026 the market paid 4.2x on our normalised Sep-28E core profit, above the median, so the share already prices in more than ONGC's history supports. The street's 6.5-8x would give ₹295-340: the whole gap between us and the street is the multiple.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good dividend, a peak year, and a fair price only on the street's multiple

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's dominant oil and gas producer, earning ~₹29.9 a share of core profit at ~US$70 Brent (Sep-28E), plus listed stakes worth ₹80 a share, ONGC Videsh and unlisted holdings. A peak FY27E (EPS ₹{{F.eps.0|n1}}) pays a large dividend.

**What you are paying:** ₹225.8, i.e. 4.2x our Sep-28E core profit after the stakes, above the 3.3x median the market has paid since 2021. Our target {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). The street's ₹296 median needs 6.5-8x.

segments.name: ONGC standalone (domestic E&P)
segments._why: Growth and margin are copied from the build below by ONGC.val.js (see 'build'). FY26 revenue Rs132,506 cr (crude 63%, gas 27%, value-added products 9%); EBITDA margin 46.6% after exploration write-offs. Q1FY27: revenue +45% to Rs46,460 cr, margin 61% at US$99.45/bbl.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in the segment
assumptions._unallocWhy: Single business: all costs are in the segment.

build._baseWhy: FY26 actuals (AR FY26 ten-year table): crude Rs83,810 cr on 18.79 MMT sold, gas Rs36,330 cr on 15.491 BCM; Brent US$70.45 (AR MD&A), INR/US$ 88.31 (PPAC). Gas US$7.3/mmBtu = average 'overall' realisation of the FY26 quarters (JM: US$7.1-7.6). Each line scales with volume, price and the rupee.
build._crudeVolWhy: Q1FY27 crude production -5% YoY (KG-98/2 reservoir problems, Western Offshore pipeline work, well shut-ins during project hook-ups); management expects oil to recover to about last year's level by year-end and +~0.5 MMT in FY28 (half of the ~1 MMTOE FY28 gain). PL cut FY27E standalone oil to 18.9 MMT production (-2%).
build._brentWhy: FY27E: Q1 ~US$97.5 (management), Jul-Sep ~US$96, then the EIA Sep-2026 path (US$90 in 2H2026, ~US$85 in Q1-2027). FY28E: EIA's US$77 in Q2-2027 and ~US$67 in 2H2027 and after. FY29E: US$70, between EIA's 2027 exit and management's US$75+ long-run view. The street uses US$80 FY27E and US$70-75 from FY28E. Realisation tracks Brent (contracts with refiners at a small premium; Q1FY27 US.45 vs Brent ~US-98).
build._fxWhy: Rupee ~95.4/US$ in Aug-2026 (JM key data) vs 88.31 FY26 average; we assume ~1.5% a year depreciation thereafter.
build._gasVolWhy: Q1FY27 gas sales 3.7 BCM (-4% YoY; offtake problems at isolated fields). New gas from DUDP (+2 mmscmd by Dec-26), East Coast CPP (1.3), Tapti/Daman (0.5) and KG-98/2 (3 mmscmd by Q4FY27, 6-7 by Q4FY28): management guides +1 BCM in FY27 production and ~+0.5 MMTOE gas in FY28. PL: FY28E gas production 20.4 BCM (+5%).
build._gasPriceWhy: Q1FY27 US$9.2 overall (APM capped at US$7.00, new-well gas US$13.31 on 24% of sales). FY27E: formula price US$9.0 in Sep-2026 falls with crude, so new-well gas (1.2x the formula, uncapped) eases to ~US$10-11: US$8.7 average. FY28-29E: at ~US$70 crude the formula (10% of the Indian basket) is ~US$7.0, at or below the US$7.25-7.50 ceiling; new-well gas ~US$8.4 on 28-30% of volumes: ~US$7.8 overall.
build._vapWhy: LPG, naphtha, ethane-propane: FY26 Rs11,879 cr; Q1FY27 ~Rs3,830 cr (JM) at US$97 crude. Scaled with crude and the rupee.
build._cessWhy: OIDB cess (charged on nomination crude) = 15.55% of crude revenue in FY26 (Rs13,034 cr).
build._royaltyWhy: Royalty was 10.8% of crude and gas revenue in FY26 (Rs12,965 cr). Cut from 8-May-2026: offshore crude 9.09%->8%, gas 10%->8% (onland nomination crude restored to 16.66% on 4-Jun-2026): about -1.1 point on the FY27 mix, for ~10.5 months of FY27.
build._leviesWhy: National calamity duty ~Rs86 cr; no windfall tax (SAED abolished Dec-2024, not re-imposed by 30-Sep-2026; bear case adds it back).
build._opexWhy: FY26 Rs28,209 cr (+2.7%). Q1FY27 ~Rs6,500 cr. +5% in FY27E (rupee weakness lifts dollar-linked rig and vessel costs), +4.5% a year after.
build._explWhy: Survey plus dry wells: FY25 Rs9,826 cr, FY26 Rs9,729 cr (Q4FY26 dry wells Rs5,110 cr). Q1FY27 low (dry wells Rs1,108 cr; surveys delayed by retendering) but management expects a big post-monsoon survey programme and more deepwater wells (Rs800-1,000 cr each) under Samudra Manthan.
build._otherWhy: Provisions and write-offs (FY26 Rs3,948 cr) plus exchange loss (Rs2,699 cr) and other items: Rs6,702 cr in FY26. Q1FY27 implies ~Rs1,100 cr a quarter; the rupee's fall keeps FY27 high.

assumptions._capexWhy: Guidance US$3.5-4.0 bn a year (Rs33,000-38,000 cr at Rs95); FY26 Rs35,878 cr. The engine adds capex to the gross block and the cost build already expenses dry wells, so we enter capex less ~Rs8,500-10,000 cr of exploratory wells that end up written off: Rs35,000 / 36,500 / 37,500 cr of total spend.
assumptions._depWhy: Depletion, depreciation and amortisation (incl. impairment) Rs25,134 cr in FY26; Q1FY27 Rs6,283 cr (Rs25,100 cr a year). Rate set so FY27E is ~Rs25,500 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Other income is built (below), not a yield on 'treasury', because the engine's treasury here also holds the stakes at book value.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: FY26 Rs10,356 cr = interest Rs4,051 cr (bank deposits Rs2,174 cr on Rs28,660 cr cash; site-restoration fund Rs1,617 cr) + dividends Rs4,807 cr (HPCL 1,811, IOC+GAIL 2,202, MRPL 502, Petronet 188, OVL 51, PMHB 53) + other Rs1,498 cr. TTM Jun-26 Rs11,007 cr; Q1FY27 Rs1,861 cr (no dividends in Q1). FY27E: interest 4,100 + dividends 4,000 (HPCL's Q1 loss rules out interims) + other 1,500; FY28E 4,300 + 4,200 + 1,500; FY29E 4,500 + 4,500 + 1,500.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs4,529 cr, Q1FY27 Rs1,086 cr: mostly interest on Rs25,822 cr of lease liabilities (rigs, vessels); borrowings only Rs7,823 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Statutory 25.17%; dividends received are deductible under section 80M, so the effective rate is ~25.17% x (PBT - dividends) / PBT. Set by ONGC.val.js from the build.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 DPS Rs13.25 (interims Rs6.00 and Rs6.25 plus a final) = 51% of EPS (Rs16,669 cr); FY24-25 38-43%. With FY27E profit ~75% higher we assume a 40% payout (MOSL 38%): DPS rises, the ratio falls.

dcf._betaWhy: A commodity producer with state ownership: market-like sensitivity; cost of equity 12.5%. Debt is small (borrowings Rs7,823 cr), so the cost of equity is used as the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: Mature, depleting fields: 1% nominal terminal growth (house range 5-6% is for growing businesses). ONGC 1P reserves (518 MMtoe) are ~13 years of FY26 output; it holds production flat only with continuous capex, so we fade growth to 1%.
dcf._fadeWhy: Margin fades to 45% (FY26 47% at US crude, before any windfall tax); capex to 20% of revenue (FY24-26 ~25% incl. written-off wells); depreciation 17% of revenue (FY26 19%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Brent stays near US$80 after the Hormuz premium (management's US$75+ view); KG-98/2 and the Western Offshore projects lift output ~4% a year; no windfall tax; the market keeps a 20% holding discount and values OVL at MOSL's ₹23 a share.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Brent falls to ~US$60 as EIA's 2H2027 surplus deepens, or a windfall tax returns; output stays flat; HPCL's losses deepen and the holding discount widens to 25% (MOSL, PL); OVL at JM's ₹7 a share; OPaL worth nothing.

parts.name: ONGC standalone (core): P/E on Sep-28E core profit
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E core profit (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E, before dividends from the stakes) ₹37,610 cr × 3.5x (bull 5.5x on ₹47,076 cr, bear 2.5x on ₹26,922 cr)
parts.note: ONGC's own implied forward P/E on core profit since Apr-2021 (median 3.3x), times the +2.2% oil-and-gas sector move at 30-Sep-2026.

parts.name: MRPL: 71.63% stake at market
parts.note: Subsidiary (HPCL holds a further 16.96%); AR FY26 note 11.1.

parts.name: Less: holding discount on the listed stakes
parts.metricLabel: Base 20%, bull 20%, bear 25% of the listed stakes
parts.note: House rule for listed stakes inside an operating company: 20% unless the street clearly differs (JM and BOB 20%, MOSL and PL 25%, Geojit 50%).

parts.name: ONGC Videsh (100%)
parts.metricLabel: ₹15 a share: midpoint of JM (7x FY28E EPS, ₹7) and MOSL (0.5x FY25 book, ₹23); bull MOSL, bear JM
parts.note: Overseas E&P; Sakhalin-1 restored from Jan-2026; ONGC cost ₹15,000 cr.

parts.name: Other unlisted subsidiaries, JVs and associates at cost
parts.metricLabel: OPaL ₹21,181 cr, ONGC Green ₹4,700 cr, others ₹1,711 cr (bear: OPaL at zero)

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values ONGC (JM, MOSL, PL, Geojit): standalone on P/E plus the stakes.

methods.name: P/E on standalone EPS
methods.why: ONGC's own one-year-forward P/E on reported standalone EPS since Apr-2021: median 5.5x (no trough years in the window), times the 2.2% sector move: 5.5x. It prices the stakes through their dividends, at ONGC's multiple.

methods.name: DCF (standalone, plus investments at book)
methods.why: Standalone free cash flow; the engine's net cash includes ONGC's investments at book value (cost for subsidiaries, fair value for IOC and GAIL).
